# QS-CFW-3173-95 Quality specification - gear blank CFW-3173-95 (8620)

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P1  
Parts: CFW-3173-95

Scope
- This quality specification defines the metallurgical, dimensional, and inspection acceptance criteria for gear blank CFW-3173-95 (CFW-3173-95) produced in Plant P1. It applies to all forged deliveries of the part number listed above and to internal transfers for machining and heat treatment. The specification focuses on requirements necessary to ensure downstream gear manufacture and service performance for forged 8620 material supplied as blank form.

Background and rationale
- The requirements are derived from service load considerations for gears and from historical process capability for the forging and rough-bore operations. The hardness requirement balances core toughness and surface strength after subsequent heat treatment and machining. The bore tolerance supports accurate mounting and minimizes rework at the machining center. The maximum forging weight is controlled to match press capacity and tooling design limits; exceeding this weight risks improper die fill and dimensional deviation.
- Examples: A blank that meets the hardness requirement but has a bore outside tolerance will be rejected for machining because it can induce runout in finish gear cutting. A blank within bore tolerance but above the maximum forging weight will be segregated to prevent damage to press tooling and die alignment.

Requirements table

| Characteristic | Requirement | Acceptance criteria / Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Chemical / material | 8620 forging charge per material control records | Material certificate must accompany each lot. |
| Hardness (core, as-forged or post-forging, pre-heat-treat if applicable) | The hardness range for gear blank CFW-3173-95 (CFW-3173-95) is 37-43 HRC. | Measured on cross-section surface prepared per Inspection Method. Readings outside this range are nonconforming. |
| Bore diameter tolerance | The bore diameter tolerance for gear blank CFW-3173-95 (CFW-3173-95) is ±0.03 mm. | Tolerance applies to nominal bore dimension indicated on manufacturing drawing. Measurement method per Inspection Method. |
| Forging weight | The maximum forging weight for gear blank CFW-3173-95 (CFW-3173-95) is 100.6 kg. | Weight recorded on heat/lot tag. Blanks exceeding this weight are nonconforming for die and press capacity reasons. |
| Surface condition | Free of forging laps, cold shuts, and metal flow interruptions that affect machinability | Visual and tactile inspection criteria per Inspection Method. |

Inspection method
- Sample selection: Inspect all first-piece blanks from a new billet lot and then sample per lot transfer records. Maintain lot traceability on the heat/lot tag with forging weight recorded.
- Hardness measurement:
  - Prepare a representative cross-section by removing scale and cleaning the test surface to expose metal. Use a Rockwell hardness tester appropriate for HRC scale. Ensure indent locations avoid surface decarburization and are at a consistent depth from the as-forged surface as practical.
  - Record each reading with the lot identifier and operator initials. The lot is conforming only if recorded readings fall within The hardness range for gear blank CFW-3173-95 (CFW-3173-95) is 37-43 HRC.
- Bore measurement:
  - Use calibrated bore gauges compatible with the bore feature. Measure at multiple circumferential positions to detect out-of-round. Record the nominal dimension and tolerance and verify The bore diameter tolerance for gear blank CFW-3173-95 (CFW-3173-95) is ±0.03 mm.
  - If the bore is produced as a rough-bore during forging, ensure the recorded rough-bore dimensions allow final machining within tolerance; otherwise, segregate the part.
- Weight verification:
  - Weigh each forged blank on a calibrated scale and record the value on the heat/lot tag and inspection record. Verify that the recorded value does not exceed The maximum forging weight for gear blank CFW-3173-95 (CFW-3173-95) is 100.6 kg.
- Surface and visual inspection:
  - Inspect for forging defects that could compromise machinability or performance. Document findings and photograph any suspect areas referenced to the lot tag.

Nonconformance handling
- Segregation and identification:
  - Any blank failing the hardness, bore tolerance, or maximum forging weight requirements must be immediately segregated and tagged with a nonconformance tag referencing this document id.
- Disposition options and rationale:
  - Hardness out of range: Evaluate whether the deviation is due to surface decarburization or process variation. If the nonconformance is surface-limited and removable by machining without compromising part geometry or subsequent treatments, document the evaluation and the agreed disposition with quality engineering; otherwise, reject the part for return to melt/remanufacture.
  - Bore out of tolerance: Reject for machining; if the deviation is minor and documented evidence shows downstream machining can restore compliance without reducing fatigue life or functional fit, a documented disposition may be approved by quality engineering and process engineering.
  - Weight over maximum forging weight: Reject and prevent shipment. Blanks exceeding The maximum forging weight for gear blank CFW-3173-95 (CFW-3173-95) is 100.6 kg must be returned to forging operations for investigation of billet size, forge programming, and die setup adjustments.
- Records to keep:
  - Maintain inspection records for hardness measurements, bore measurements, and weighing with the lot identifier. Keep nonconformance tags and disposition documentation with the lot file. Retain photographic evidence for significant defects and the approval record for any authorized concessions.
- Corrective action:
  - For repeated nonconformances from the same lot source or process step, initiate a formal corrective action to address root cause, including but not limited to forging process setup, material charge control, and equipment calibration. Document actions taken and results, and attach to the lot file.

Traceability and records
- Each blank must retain heat/lot identification from forging through inspection and shipment. Inspection records must reference the lot identifier and be filed in the plant quality system. Records include hardness logs, bore measurement sheets showing The bore diameter tolerance for gear blank CFW-3173-95 (CFW-3173-95) is ±0.03 mm, weight logs showing The maximum forging weight for gear blank CFW-3173-95 (CFW-3173-95) is 100.6 kg, and nonconformance documentation where applicable.

End of specification.
